title: Macro-regime overlay on equal-weight BTC/ETH (VIX, Treasury curve, NFCI, SOFR/EFFR, DFF) vs price-only baselines
mechanism: Eight predeclared daily state rules (one variable or a two-variable conjunction each) gate an equal-weight BTC/ETH spot long/cash allocation. When the rule is ON the basket is held 50/50; when OFF the account sits in cash. Decisions are made at 00:00 UTC of each crypto day using only macro observations whose publication lags have fully elapsed, and the day's basket return is earned by the position decided that morning (next-bar execution). Development (2020-08-01..2023-12-31) selects one frozen rule by net Sharpe at 1x costs; validation (2024) is a single frozen pass. No macro variable, in any of the eight predeclared forms, added information over the internal price-only trend baseline, and the development-selected rule underperformed both the equal-weight buy-and-hold benchmark and its own price-only baseline in validation.

crypto: Binance BTCUSDT spot 1h klines 2020-08..2024-12 (daily mark = 23:00-24:00 UTC bar close; manifest-verified SHA-256, rows, member lists)
macro: CBOE VIX_History.csv daily close (cross-checked equal to FRED VIXCLS on all 1277 overlapping 2020-2024 dates)
FRED T10Y2Y 10Y-2Y constant-maturity spread (source H.15) via fred_regime_bundle.zip/daily.csv
FRED DFF effective federal funds rate (daily,_7-day.csv member despite name; values are daily DFF)
NY Fed SOFR and EFFR daily (nyfed_sofr_2020-01-01_2026-08-28.csv, nyfed_effr_2020-01-01_2026-08-28.csv)

revision_and_lag_caveats.vix: CBOE VIX close for date D publishes ~21:15 UTC on D. Cutoffs use the previous US business day, leaving <= ~9 hours to the next-day 00:00 UTC decision plus a buffer, so same-late-day publication is respected with slack. VIX is computed from SPX option quotes only; it is an equity-implied stress proxy, not a crypto-specific volatility measure, and its level regime is ETH/BTC-agnostic. CBOE records VIX values as final (no revision policy); historical files can be superseded by CBOE data corrections. CBOE terms: personal/non-commercial internal research only, no redistribution.
revision_and_lag_caveats.t10y2y: H.15/FRED T10Y2Y for D publishes the same day (~21:00 UTC); cutoff = previous US business day. Treasuries occasionally restate H.15 values after publication; the study treats the collected snapshot as final. On US federal holidays there is no quote and the prior business day's value carries forward (criterion evaluated on the last published value, which is public by construction). One 2020-05-20 T10Y2Y outlier (2.38) was treated as a genuine quote, as published.
revision_and_lag_caveats.dff: FRED DFF for D is published the NEXT US business day ~13:00 UTC; one extra business day beyond the cutoff is enforced (lag offset -1). DFF is a backward-average of overnight federal funds trades and is periodically restated by FRED; the settled value lag is robust to such restatements.
revision_and_lag_caveats.sofr_effr: NY Fed SOFR/EFFR for D publish the NEXT US business day ~13:00 UTC; extra business day enforced (offset -1). The NY Fed's volume-weighted distribution stats can be revised after first publication (Revision Indicator column was empty throughout the collected file); the headline rate used here is normally settled at publication. SOFR still displays occasional outliers from month-end/quarter-end repo dynamics;
revision_and_lag_caveats.nfci: Chicago Fed NFCI is weekly (value dated the week-ending Friday) and is published the FOLLOWING Wednesday ~14:30 UTC (+3 business days). With the 00:00 UTC decision boundary this requires a 4-business-day publication offset, which run.py enforces. Chicago Fed explicitly revises the most recent weeks of NFCI history with each release; values used here can differ from the vintages a trader saw at the time by small amounts, and the rule threshold (negative) is close to zero where revisions matter, so NFCI-based point-in-time validity is qualified rather than exact-current-vintage.
revision_and_lag_caveats._general: All series are reindexed to US business days (USFederalHolidayCalendar) and forward-filled before shifting, and every observable enters at its enforced publication lag: same-late-day publishers at cutoff = previous business day; next-morning publishers at cutoff minus one additional business day; NFCI at cutoff minus four business days. No series containing observations dated after 2024-12-31 was loaded or read (files are sliced at --end before any computation).

parameters.universe: equal-weight 50/50 BTC/ETH USDT spot, long/cash only, no leverage, no borrowing

frozen_rules.t2_vix_hyst: ON when VIX <= 25; OFF when VIX >= 32; else hold previous state (init OFF)
frozen_rules.t4_curve_hyst: ON when T10Y2Y >= +0.05; OFF when T10Y2Y <= -0.05; else hold previous (init OFF)
frozen_rules.t7_trend_veto: ON iff (basket close > its 31-day SMA, evaluated on the PRIOR day's close/SMA) AND NOT (VIX > 30 AND T10Y2Y < 0)
frozen_rules.t8_policy_easing: ON iff DFF fell over the trailing 20 US business days

parameters.selection_rule: Highest development net Sharpe at 1x costs (12 bps/leg one-way); tie-break lower development turnover, then lexicographic id. Selection used development data only.

signal_timing.decision: 00:00 UTC of each crypto day t
signal_timing.macro_observables: as-of the last US business day strictly before t, minus the per-series publication offset (0 for VIX/T10Y2Y, 1 extra business day for DFF/SOFR/EFFR, 4 business days for NFCI)
signal_timing.price_observables: crypto daily marks (23:00 UTC closes) through t-1 only; trend conditions compare the t-1 close to the t-1 SMA31
signal_timing.trade: position for day t is set at t 00:00 UTC and earns day t's basket return; recounts as next-bar execution
signal_timing.hysteresis_init: states initialize OFF at the panel start (conservative)

cost_model.applied: cost = 2 legs x |exposure_change| x 12 bps charged on the decision day; the initial position (from zero) is charged identically for overlays and benchmarks
cost_model.cash_yield_note: cash accrues 0 in the headline results (conservative); a sensitivity run crediting SOFR on cash days moved the selected trial's validation net Sharpe from 0.877 to 0.929 and left the cumulative excess vs buy-and-hold negative (-0.470), so the conclusion is insensitive to cash yield
cost_model.benchmark_entry_cost_note: the buy-and-hold benchmark pays its one-time entry cost (2 legs x 12 bps = 24 bps), which slightly reduces it relative to a pure buy-and-hold (48 bps total effect over validation is sub-percent of the 83% benchmark return; immaterial to every comparison)

also_reported: internal price-only trend baseline: hold basket iff prior-day basket close > its 31-day SMA (bench_trend31; the price-only twin of t7 with the macro veto removed)
SOFR cash accrual while in cash, reported as sensitivity only

selected_trial_t7_trend_veto.drawdown_change_vs_bench_2024: +7.1pp deeper ( -0.426 vs -0.355 ): the overlay added drawdown while forfeiting return
selected_trial_t7_trend_veto.missed_upside_2024: 34 states-off days forfeited an arithmetic 1.71x of daily basket gains and 0.30 of linear benchmark return; the binding event was the 2024 Q1 melt-up that began from below the SMA

t5_nfci_neg.note: state never OFF in either window (NFCI stayed negative); degenerate copy of buy-and-hold

t6_stress_veto.note: veto fired once in dev, never in validation

all_trials_validation_2024.reading: No trial beat buy-and-hold on net Sharpe with nonnegative 2x-cost excess. The two curve gates cut 2024 drawdown roughly in half (-0.14 vs -0.355) but at massive missed upside (cum_excess -0.25..-0.35), so they fail the risk-overlay alternative (lower drawdown at comparable return) as well; their flat-in-cash periods also carried several 2024-leg-leading downside days mis-signed (drawdown improvement at deeply negative excess is not a refundable edge). NFCI's threshold never binds in a 2020-2024 ZIRP/UKR regime where the index stays negative throughout, making t5 uninformative rather than successful; the same degeneracy holds for the SOFR-EFFR spread (constant near zero), which is why no rule was predicated on it.

metrics.internal_baseline_comparison: The price-only SMA31 baseline itself DECAYED in validation (dev 1.30 -> val 0.877 net Sharpe; it also lagged buy-and-hold in 2024): the macro overlay was selected because t7==trend31 in dev within construction noise; in validation they are observationally identical (0 differing days). Macro conditions added no incremental signal over their price-only twin in either window.

first_falsification_gate.definition: Contract gate applied to the development-selected rule on the 2024 validation window: G1 >= 100 net observations; G2 validation net Sharpe > 0 AND > named benchmark (equal-weight BTC/ETH buy-and-hold); G3 cumulative validation excess vs benchmark >= 0 at 2x costs; G4 no timing/universe/future-data leakage (point-in-time reconstruction checks); G5 rule-budget respected (<=8 rules; a risk-overlay alternative would require lower drawdown at comparable return).

G4_no_leakage.value: 0 mismatches in as-of values, rule states, and panel dating across 12 sampled reconstruction points

leakage_checks.point_in_time_reconstruction: For 12 sampled decision dates spanning 2020-2024, every macro input series was truncated to observations with date <= the decision cutoff (with the series-specific publication offsets), the as-of value and the entire boolean state history were rebuilt from truncated inputs, and both were compared to the full-run computation: zero mismatches.
leakage_checks.panel_dating: Daily crypto marks use the close of the 23:00-24:00 UTC bar (the day's final bar); 2026 microsecond-epoch files are auto-detected but none were read in wave one (slice at --end precedes parsing).
leakage_checks.future_data_guard: run.py fails closed when --end > 2024-12-31 unless QUANT_HOLDOUT_UNLOCK=1 is set; wave-one runs used no flag; series are sliced at --end before computation; no file fields beyond the end date are parsed.
leakage_checks.next_bar_execution: Position for day t is decided at 00:00 UTC and earns day t's return; trend conditions reference the t-1 close and t-1 SMA (an initial implementation used day-t closes and was caught by the reconstruction check and fixed before results were frozen)
leakage_checks.revise_vintage_caveat: NFCI and (rarely) H.15/NY-Fed rates are retrospectively revisable; NFCI's 4-business-day publication lag defends against look-ahead, but exact trader-vintage replication is not guaranteed, and this limitation is a primary reason results are reported as falsified-with-caveats rather than evidence about true current-vintage signals.

risks: Result breadth is limited: the conclusion falsifies these eight simple state rules, not the existence of any macro-crypto regime link; the 2020-2024 window contains essentially one macro cycle (ZIRP-to-hikes-to-cuts) and one 2024 ETF-driven bull in which macro states simply did not bind.

NFCI and rate-spread rules are degenerate in this sample (never or almost never OFF), so their true out-of-sample behavior is unidentified from this exercise; the SOFR-EFFR spread was never predicated on for this reason, and the absence of a t5' variant is a designed non-test, not evidence against NFCI generally.

Threshold sensitivity was not re-swept after freezing (by protocol); dev Sharpe margins between top rules are small (1.32 vs 1.03 runner-up) and the winner's dev edge came mostly from its price term, as shown by the identical price-only twin.
CBOE VIX terms allow non-commercial internal research only; the collected file is not redistributable, and VIX is an equity-implied proxy which conceptually cannot measure crypto-specific stress.

Cost model is a research assumption (12 bps/leg plus 2x stress per contract), not the user's fee tier; conclusions on the shortfall are robust to 2x costs but the absolute turnover (68 two-leg units in 2024) would be materially costlier at retail taker rates.

The 2024 buy-and-hold benchmark exception was large (+83% with -35.5% max drawdown); any risk-improvement framing must also survive the fact that curve gates achieved lower drawdown (-14%) only with deeply negative excess (-25..-35pp), which the protocol rejects as an overlay-pass tradeoff.
next_experiment: Drop single-macro gates on crypto return prediction. If macro data is pursued further, the defensible direction from this dossier is narrower: (a) test whether joint-stress days (VIX>30 AND inverted curve; only ~13 dev days, 1 validation day) trigger short-lived crypto drawdown continuation worth a TACTICAL (hours-to-days) de-risking rather than a binary day-level state, and (b) only with exact current-vintage series (e.g., NFCI vintage archive) revisit weekly-frequency state rules. Neither precedes the price-only trend baseline's own 2024 decay, which is the more actionable finding for this universe.
